subject: Request: Adjusted completion commitment for nightly batch inference (VectorMed)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@vectormed.com>

Cc: VectorMed Procurement <procurement@vectormed.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly batch completion window — request for adjusted commitment

Hi Evelyn,

We're getting close to go-live for our nightly QC pipeline that runs ~2.1M inference ops per night against a mix of short and very long sequences. Over the last two weeks we've observed a tail where 1.8% of nightly jobs slip past the 02:00 UTC completion window you outlined. 

Our legal and ops teams are asking whether Redwood can provide a formal amendment for our contract that: 1) acknowledges a longer finalization window for scheduled nightly bulk jobs (we're proposing up to a 4-hour grace window), 2) prescribes a safe retry/backoff pattern and idempotency expectations so consumers can safely retry without creating duplicates, and 3) defines credits or remediation when completion > tolerance.

Can you confirm what tradeoffs you need on routing/priority/quantization to support that and whether an addendum is possible for the RDW-3482 purchase? If helpful, attach our run profile and a sample job trace and we can share more details.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Data Platform — VectorMed
[sent from mobile]

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch completion window — request for adjusted commitment

Samira — thanks for the clear summary. We can put together an amendment, but want to align on three practical knobs and one guardrail: 

- Window extension: we can support a contractual 4-hour completion envelope for scheduled nightly bulk jobs (e.g., jobs started as part of the "nightly" schedule).
- Safe retry & idempotency: require a request-level idempotency key (client-provided) and idempotency window (we propose 72 hours) to avoid duplicate side effects.
- Backoff & retry guidance: recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a maximum of 5 retries for async job submission; server-side backpressure signals will be surfaced in the job status API.
- Guardrail (SLA credits): propose a tiered credit model — first 1% of jobs beyond the envelope: no credit (we absorb), next 3%: 2% monthly usage credit, >4%: escalation and review with potential larger credit (negotiable).

I've attached a draft SLO matrix that maps job size/priority to routing policies and suggested safe-retry patterns. Please review and we'll iterate to match VectorMed's operational tolerance.

Attachments: [attachment: slo_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]

— Evelyn

Subject: Proposed amendment: Nightly bulk completion envelope (RDW-3482)

Hi Samira — following up with a proposed amendment and a short implementation plan. Summary of the proposed terms below; attached is the exhibit (redwood-delta-commit-exhibit.pdf) and a DocuSign packet if you want to sign.

Proposed terms (high level):
1) Completion envelope: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure scheduled nightly bulk inference jobs are marked Completed within 4 hours of scheduled window end (the "Envelope"). The baseline SLA remains the same for on-demand/interactive requests.

2) Idempotency & safe retries: Client must provide a client-side idempotency key for each logical job. Redwood will deduplicate submissions bearing the same key within a 72-hour idempotency window. For job-level retries, Redwood will surface deterministic job ids and a job-status API; clients should use exponential backoff with jitter and a maximum of 5 retries.

3) Routing and priority: To meet the Envelope, Redwood may re-route scheduled nightly jobs to batch-optimized pools, apply quantization profiles, or schedule work within reserved time-slices. If VectorMed requires guaranteed dedicated capacity for nightly runs, that is available under a Dedicated contract amendment.

4) Credits & remediation: Monthly credits will be applied if the fraction of nightly jobs that miss the Envelope exceeds 2% in a calendar month. Credit scale: 2–5% missed -> 2% usage credit; >5% missed -> 5% usage credit plus joint post-mortem. Repeated >10% misses in two consecutive months triggers commercial review.

5) Exceptions: Jobs flagged as "non-retriable" or any job causing downstream side-effects must be explicitly declared at submission; such jobs are excluded from the Envelope and treated as on-demand requests.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood-delta-commit-exhibit.pdf (pdf, 128 KB)]
Links: DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/packet/RDW-3482-exhibit
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/3482

2) Can you confirm that the 72-hour idempotency window applies to job-level dedup only and not to token-level caching? (We will keep an internal mapping but want clarity.)
